body:
CHIEF: HOLD ON 6562c88, and it is a SEQUENCING problem rather than a quality one. One blocker
is unaddressed at this SHA, and I verified it in the candidate's own source rather than
inferring it from the review thread.

  document/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/document/compiler.scala

    ~1463    finding.note.getOrElse("")
    ~1487    call.promptTemplateVersion.getOrElse("")

Both still collapse None and Some("") to the identical rendering. That is exactly the collision
codex-storymodel-collab raised at 19:20 and I upheld as a blocker at 19:23 -- after your B5/B6/M1
closures, which is why your landing request lists three blockers closed and not four. You have
not ignored it; it landed on you mid-flight.

WHY IT STILL BLOCKS, restated because it is the least intuitive of the four: everything else we
have fixed today was a value claiming MORE than it knew. This is an identity claiming LESS than
it must. A content address that cannot separate two distinct inputs is not a weak address, it is
not an address -- and a change from None to Some("") is invisible to the very mechanism built to
notice change. You now fingerprint full emitted ClaimMeta, which makes the fingerprint MORE
load-bearing, so a collision inside it matters more than it did an hour ago, not less.

THE FIX IS TWO FIELDS AND collab HAS ALREADY BOUNDED IT FOR YOU. Its adjacent-renderer audit
checked every other fold("") site and showed each is injective because its input is validated or
typed -- nonempty SpanSet, numeric scores and seeds, validated-nonblank calibration model and
predicate frame, nonempty opaque ids, an enum aspect. Exactly these two are unvalidated. So this
is not an encoder audit; it is two fields.

AND FIX THE VALUE, NOT THE RENDERER, per my disposition: make Some("") unconstructible --
canonicalize to None or reject -- rather than making two renderers cleverer. The reason the other
sites are safe is that their INPUTS are validated, not that their renderers are careful. A careful
renderer is a property of one function and dies the moment someone writes a second one. Unless
you can show Some("") carries meaning for a real provider, in which case say where and encode
injectively instead.

EVIDENCE I WANT WITH THE NEXT SHA: a law asserting the PROPERTY -- that the ambiguous value is
unconstructible, or that the two fingerprints differ -- not a test that today's pair happens to
encode distinctly.

EVERYTHING ELSE IS READY AND I WANT THAT SAID PLAINLY. 4,063 tests across JVM/JS/Native plus
grakern and bench at exit 0, reference scope 549 JVM green, scalafmtCheckAll run separately last
at 0, no path overlap with main since 75fd2a3 so your exact gate is still valid. The mutation
evidence is the strongest on the board today: causal Hypothesized -> LinguisticallyEntailed killed
1/20, causal resolution under a weaker SituationMention policy killed 3/20 by the no-default and
gap laws, and exact production restoration back to 20/20. That is a mutation that COMPILES,
fails the NAMED assertion, and restores clean -- the full standard, met twice.

And you kept the vertical claim precisely worded: one-sentence WOG mechanical reachability via an
honestly named deterministic fixture provider, explicitly not an answered research question. That
sentence is going to be repeated by me to the owner and it will survive the repetition because you
wrote it carefully.

Typed licensing follow-on filed as bd-01M17GC475EPDVW5Z4D776AYH0, as required. Good.

Two fields, one law, new SHA. I will gate immediately -- this is the critical path and I do not
want it sitting.
